annotations.summary: {{ $labels.instance }} has over 40 days uptime on macOS {{ $labels.product_version }} (Darwin {{ $labels.kernel_release }})
annotations.description: This Tahoe kernel family is at risk of the 32-bit TCP clock wraparound observed on the production fleet. Schedule a drained OS upgrade before another 49.7-day clock wrap. The alert uses OS family and uptime as risk indicators; it does not prove a frozen clock. Upgrade existing hosts to the approved fixed macOS baseline; changing the provisioning image does not upgrade existing machines. If SSH uploads are already slow, read the TCP clock runbook before rebooting: legacy installers may have truncated the live tart-kubelet executable.

model.expr: ((macos_host_uptime_seconds{job="tuist-macos-node-exporter"} > bool 3456000) * on (instance, job, cluster, env) group_left (kernel_release, product_version) macos_host_info{job="tuist-macos-node-exporter",kernel_release=~"25\\.[0-3]\\..*"}) and on (instance, job, cluster, env) (time() - node_textfile_mtime_seconds{job="tuist-macos-node-exporter",file=~".*/host_sensors.prom"} < 180)

annotations.summary: {{ $labels.instance }} has over 5000 TCP sockets in TIME_WAIT
annotations.description: TIME_WAIT sockets have remained above 5000 for 15 minutes. Correlate macos_host_info and macos_host_uptime_seconds, transfer throughput, and repeated TCP timestamp samples. On the October 26 incident, 12714 sockets accumulated on a 102-day-old Darwin 25.3.0 host with frozen TCP timestamps. High connection churn can also cause this alert; the count alone does not prove a kernel bug.

model.expr: (macos_host_tcp_time_wait{job="tuist-macos-node-exporter"} > bool 5000) and on (instance, job, cluster, env) (time() - node_textfile_mtime_seconds{job="tuist-macos-node-exporter",file=~".*/host_sensors.prom"} < 180)

annotations.summary: {{ $labels.instance }} cannot report fresh macOS host health
annotations.description: Host sysctl/netstat collection is failing, or host_sensors.prom is older than three minutes. Check launchctl print system/dev.tuist.host-sensors and /var/log/tuist-host-sensors.log. OS/uptime and TCP risk alerts require fresh readings; this alert covers failed commands and a stopped one-shot job while node_exporter still serves the file. A missing exporter or a file that has never existed must be handled by target availability/rollout checks.

model.expr: max by (instance, job, cluster, env) ((macos_host_health_collection_success{job="tuist-macos-node-exporter"} == bool 0) or (time() - node_textfile_mtime_seconds{job="tuist-macos-node-exporter",file=~".*/host_sensors.prom"} > bool 180))

title: Runner macOS host health collection failing
